properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. OVERLAP FIX 2026-09-14: a project-wide overlap audit found this block spatially overlapping Potrero Power Station Block 3/4 in real-world coordinates near the two sites' shared border -- a genuine disagreement between Pier 70's and Potrero's independent transforms, not a same-site priority call. Clipped back from Potrero's blocks, since Potrero's transform was independently validated against real building bearings (Sophie Maxwell/UCSF) earlier in this project, while this specific southern edge of Pier 70 has not been satellite-verified. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): a batch color-region check found this block's committed shape was roughly 55-85m too far south and too wide versus the diagram's actual fill. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) across the combined H1/H2 area, split at the real internal divider (the dashed sub-division line at pixel x~1701-1746, using its midpoint x~1723 as the H1/H2 boundary), and extracted this block's own contour (OpenCV) including its real diagonal NE corner (matching the shoreline curve) at pixel (1723,1300), (1974,1300), (1974,1329), (1918,1462), (1723,1462). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. This also discards a large number of redundant near-duplicate vertices left over from the 2026-09-14 Potrero-boundary clip, no longer needed since this new, smaller shape does not reach that boundary at all (re-confirmed zero overlap with Potrero Block 3/4). CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (street/curb re-anchoring pass, prompted by a user question about validation process consistency): this block's own north edge was directly confirmed, by rendering it against Esri World Imagery, to sit on top of real, currently-paved, actively-used street pavement (visible lane markings and/or vehicles in the satellite image), not a corner-lot sliver -- one of several Pier 70 blocks found this way after this project switched its real-street reference from OSM (community-traced, name-matched ways) to DataSF's own official Street Centerline / Curbs and Islands datasets (src/street_geometry.py), which for the first time gave an accurate enough curb position to see it. Clipped via shapely difference() against the corrected real-street buffer (6.8m centerline half-width, empirically measured against real curb data near Pier 70 -- see street_geometry.py); area 3557 -> 2185 sq m. The clip's result was a MultiPolygon (the street cut disconnected a 351 sq m sliver from the main body); kept only the larger piece, consistent with how this project has handled the same situation elsewhere (Mission Rock Square, Potrero Block 7). This is a targeted correction of this block's street-facing edge, not a re-verified re-trace of its other edges, which still carry this site's usual diagram-transform uncertainty.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data -- see digitization_method.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Office, 90 ft max per Figure 6.4.2, same combined ~430,000 RSF program as Parcel H1 (see that entry). No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.
